guarantees.claim: reg_hash_start is the AND of reg2hw.cmd.hash_start.qe and reg2hw.cmd.hash_start.q, producing a pulse when command and enable are both high
reg_hash_stop is the AND of reg2hw.cmd.hash_stop.qe and reg2hw.cmd.hash_stop.q
reg_hash_continue is the AND of reg2hw.cmd.hash_continue.qe and reg2hw.cmd.hash_continue.q
reg_hash_process is the AND of reg2hw.cmd.hash_process.qe and reg2hw.cmd.hash_process.q
hw2reg.err_code.de equals err_valid and hw2reg.err_code.d equals err_code, enabling latching of the error code when err_valid is asserted
hash_start is asserted only when reg_hash_start is high AND sha_en is active, cfg_block is low, and invalid_config is low
hash_continue is asserted only when reg_hash_continue is high AND sha_en is active, cfg_block is low, and invalid_config is low
hash_process is asserted only when reg_hash_process is high AND sha_en is active, cfg_block is high, and invalid_config is low
hash_start_or_continue is the OR of hash_start and hash_continue

assumptions.claim: digest_size is a valid value of digest_mode_e and key_length is a valid value of key_length_e
assumptions.cond: when hw2reg.cfg.digest_size.d or hw2reg.cfg.key_length.d assignments are evaluated
assumptions.risk: an illegal value yields an undefined or unexpected encoding in the readback, causing software to misread the configuration and potentially use an incorrect digest/key length, compromising security

assumptions.claim: err_valid is a clean, glitch-free pulse that is asserted together with a stable err_code
assumptions.risk: glitches on err_valid or a changing err_code while err_valid is high may cause the error register to capture a wrong error code

assumptions.claim: sha_en, cfg_block, and invalid_config are stable and correctly reflect system state when a hash command pulse (reg_hash_*) occurs
assumptions.risk: a glitch or changing value may incorrectly gate the command, causing a missed hash start/continue/process or a spurious trigger, leading to operational inconsistency or security failure

assumptions.claim: Each reg2hw.cmd.hash_*.qe is a proper single-cycle pulse corresponding to a software write
assumptions.risk: if qe is not a clean single-cycle pulse, the derived reg_hash_* signals may stay high longer or glitch, causing multiple command triggers

uncertain_points.claim: digest_size and key_length may be any value written by software; if an illegal enum value is written, the casts digest_mode_e'(digest_size) and key_length_e'(key_length) will map to an unspecified encoding without any local error detection
uncertain_points.cond: when software configures an unsupported digest or key length
uncertain_points.risk: the readback may show a valid-looking encoding while hardware operates with an undefined length, potentially weakening HMAC security or enabling secret leakage

uncertain_points.claim: The qualification of hash_start/continue/process only prevents new operations when invalid_config or cfg_block is asserted; an ongoing hash operation is not aborted or flushed if an error/block condition arises mid-operation
uncertain_points.cond: when an error occurs during an active hash operation
uncertain_points.risk: secret or internal state may be processed in an unsafe configuration, leading to data corruption or key leakage

uncertain_points.claim: The combinational gating of hash_start/continue/process uses sha_en, cfg_block, invalid_config that are not synchronized to the short reg_hash_* pulse, creating a potential race condition
uncertain_points.cond: when any of the qualifying signals change simultaneously with the command pulse
uncertain_points.risk: a false positive or false negative on the command may cause missed hash operations or spurious starts, leading to state machine inconsistency

uncertain_points.claim: reg_hash_stop is generated but does not appear in any further gating within this chunk (no hash_stop signal is formed), raising a question about its usage elsewhere or if it is dead
uncertain_points.risk: if intended for an abort/halt function, the missing connection may leave the stop path broken, preventing clean shutdown of a hash operation

uncertain_points.claim: The signals sha_en, cfg_block, and invalid_config are generated by other logic; their timing contract relative to command pulses is not defined here, and any inconsistency could cause missed or incorrect command execution
uncertain_points.cond: when these external signals change asynchronously to the hash command flow
uncertain_points.risk: the command enable gating may become unreliable, potentially allowing operations in wrong modes
